input.descriptionHtml:
Formentera is the quietest of the Balearic islands, and dinner there is barefoot and unhurried: grilled fish, a salad of ripe tomatoes and a long table on a shaded terrace as the light turns gold. This sideboard brings that easy island feel to the dining room. Its doors are panelled in woven rattan, which gives a soft, sunlit texture, and its long, low top is the place to set out the bowls and platters before everyone sits down.

It is built from reclaimed oak, and its four doors open onto generous storage for plates, glasses and table linen, with a lower shelf for baskets or a row of cookbooks. At 30 inches tall it sits low and long, a shape that suits a wall beneath a window or a large painting. It arrives fully assembled.

Use it in a dining room with a big ceramic bowl and a pair of lamps on top, or in a living room for records, books and a tray of glasses. This listing is for one sideboard.

In Arezzo, the Tuscan hill town known for its monthly antiques fair, Sunday lunch is served from the side of the room: a platter of pasta, a bowl of white beans and a carafe of red, all waiting while the family finds its chairs. This sideboard is made for that kind of lunch. Four doors keep the plates, glasses and table linen close to the table, and its broad top holds every dish until the next helping.

It is made of mango wood, a dense hardwood with a lively, varied grain that makes every piece a little different, and inside, two removable shelves can be arranged around stacks of plates or taken out to make room for tall jugs and platters. It arrives fully assembled.

Give it the long wall of a dining room, with a bowl of figs, a carafe of wine and a few old prints hung above, and keep the good glasses and the everyday china behind its doors, ready for the next long lunch. This listing is for one sideboard.

input.descriptionHtml:
In Old Lyme, the American Impressionists gathered around 1900 at Florence Griswold's boarding house, where the painters talked late over supper and left their pictures on the dining room walls and doors. This sideboard is made for setting out that kind of supper. Its long, gently curved front holds the serving dishes and the wine in one easy reach, and its four doors keep a dining room's china and glasses behind them.

It is built of maple and faced in walnut veneers, quarter-cut for a straight grain and plain-sliced for a broader figure, with mitred corners, where two pieces meet at a clean angle, and brass hardware that warms against the dark wood. At more than six and a half feet long it gives a big dining room a proper serving wall. It arrives fully assembled.

Stand it along the dining room wall under a painting, with candlesticks and a bowl of fruit on top and the plates, glasses and table linens behind the doors, or use it in a living room as a long, low home for records and a lamp. This listing is for one sideboard.

At 194 lbs it is substantial and steady, and its 21-inch depth gives room behind the doors for tall bottles and stacked boards. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it in a dining room or kitchen with a cutting board, a bowl of walnuts and a lamp on top, or in a living room to hold bottles and glasses. This listing is for one cabinet.

Its three doors keep the plates, glasses and bottles together, and its broad top holds the next course and the coffee things while the table is still busy.

At six feet long it suits a dining room of almost any size. It arrives fully assembled.

Place it in a dining room with a large painting or mirror above, a ceramic bowl of lemons and a pair of lamps on top, and serving platters and table linens inside. This listing is for one sideboard.

Set it in a dining room or study with a tray of glasses and a decanter on top and a painting hung above, the bottles and spare glasses behind the doors. This listing is for one cabinet.

It is compact enough for a smaller dining room or a kitchen wall, and its four doors hold the platters, glasses and bottles a long Tuscan lunch calls for.

It is made of mango wood, and its doors are carved all over in a close pattern of linked rings, like fine metal mesh, which catches the light differently as the day moves on. At 36 inches high it is a comfortable height for serving, and at 64 inches long it gives good storage without taking over a room. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it in a dining room or a hallway with a lamp, a wooden board of cheese and a bottle of white wine ready to pour, with the good glasses kept safely behind the doors. This listing is for one sideboard.

Inside, three removable shelves can be set for stacks of plates or taken out for tall jugs. It arrives fully assembled.

Run it along a dining room or kitchen wall with earthenware bowls, a jug of wild herbs and the bread ready on top, and the everyday plates and glasses behind its doors. This listing is for one sideboard.

Set it in a living room with an ice bucket, a tray of coupes and a lamp on top and the bottles inside, or in a dining room for the china and candles. This listing is for one cabinet.

Mango wood, with its varied grain, suits the play of light across the raised panels. Behind the four doors are two removable shelves, which you can lift out for tall bottles or serving platters. At more than six and a half feet long it makes a generous serving surface. It arrives fully assembled.

Give it a dining room wall with a large bowl of lemons, a stack of plates and a pair of lamps, or set it in a living room with art books, a record player and a tray of glasses. This listing is for one sideboard.

Set it against a dining room wall under a large painting, with a lamp at either end, a bowl of fruit in the middle and a candle or two for the long summer evenings by the Strait. This listing is for one sideboard.

Stand it in a living room or dining room beneath a large painting, with a lamp, a bronze and a pile of art books on top. This listing is for one sideboard.

input.title: BH | Premier Les Baux Round Brass Wall Mirror — In Brass
input.descriptionHtml:
Les Baux sits on a rocky spur in the Alpilles of southern France, and when the north wind sweeps the sky clear, the morning light there is bright and sharp. This mirror is made for dressing in that kind of light. Round and 56 inches across, it takes in a wide sweep of the room and the window, so the last check before the door is a full one, and its rings of brass catch the sun and throw it back across the wall.

The glass is clear mirror, and the frame is built from brass plate layered in concentric circles and finished in gold, so the edge has depth and movement. At 126 lbs it is a substantial piece with real presence on a wall, and it arrives fully assembled.

Hang it in a bedroom opposite the window, above a dresser with a tray for jewellery and a small vase, or in an entry hall over a console where the light comes in through the door. This listing is for one wall mirror.

input.title: BH | Premier Poitiers Shagreen Mirror

At the twelfth-century court of Poitiers, poets and musicians gathered and dressing well was an art, and the last look before going out still matters: collar straightened, earrings checked, hair settled. This mirror is made for that look. Its frame of shagreen, a leather with a fine pebbled grain, puts a soft, polished border around your reflection, and its bevelled glass gives a clear, bright view.

The shagreen is wrapped over a sturdy board with iron, set off with handcrafted metal details in a gold tone, around mirror glass 6mm thick, so the reflection stays true. At 32 inches across it is large enough to frame your head and shoulders as you dress. It arrives fully assembled.

Hang it above a dresser or console in a bedroom or hall, with a lamp beside it and a dish for rings and earrings below, or over a vanity where the morning routine happens, with a brush and a bottle of scent close by. This listing is for one mirror.

input.descriptionHtml:
On the Riviera at Saint-Raphaël, a summer house is all about light: shutters opened early, the sea bright outside and every room as sunny as the terrace. This mirror is made to carry that light indoors. At 44 inches across it is broad enough to catch a window opposite and send the brightness back through the room, and it shows you from the head to well past the shoulders on the way out.

The glass is 6 mm thick and beveled, cut at an angle around its edge so it glints, and it is set in an octagonal frame wrapped in shagreen, a leather with a fine pebbled grain, over MDF and iron. Handmade brass details catch the light around the frame. It arrives fully assembled.

Hang it facing a window in a living room, over a fireplace or a console, where it can double the daylight, or above a dresser in a bedroom with a lamp below and a dish for earrings. This listing is for one mirror.

input.title: BH | Premier Dunmore Gilded Pineapple Mirror — In Gold
input.descriptionHtml:
The Dunmore Pineapple, the eighteenth-century stone pineapple near Falkirk, is the best-known sign of an old custom: the pineapple as a welcome to guests. This mirror carries that welcome into the hall. Crowned with a gilded pineapple, it is the last look before you open the door to friends, and at nearly six feet tall it fills an entry with light and makes even a narrow hall feel generous.

The frame is finished in gold leaf, which gives a soft, warm shine rather than a hard glitter, and the pineapple crest rises from the top of the frame. Gold leaf, beaten thinner than paper, has been used to gild frames for centuries because it catches candlelight so gently. At 79 lbs it needs secure fixings set into studs. It arrives fully assembled.

Hang it in an entry above a console with a bowl of keys and a vase of flowers, or over a dining room sideboard where it doubles the candlelight. This listing is for one mirror.

input.descriptionHtml:
Røros, the old copper-mining town high in the Norwegian mountains, is a place of wooden houses and long winters, where the hearth is the centre of every room from autumn into spring. This fire screen is made for that place by the fire. It gives the fireplace a finished face, and through the summer months, when the hearth stands empty, it keeps the dark opening dressed and tidy until the first cold evening comes around again.

It is iron in a dark finish, made up of panels that give it a strong, simple outline. At 38 inches wide and 30 high it suits most standard fireplace openings, and it stands on a slim 9-inch footprint. It works just as well as a decorative screen in a room without a fireplace, and it arrives fully assembled.

Set it in front of the hearth in a living room or bedroom, with a basket of logs to one side and candles on the mantelpiece above, or stand it in a corner as a quiet piece of ironwork. This listing is for one fire screen.

At 22 inches long it has room for a lifetime of small things, and it adds a note of polish to any surface it sits on. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it on a coffee table to tidy away the remote controls, on a dresser for watches and cufflinks, or on a bookshelf for photographs and keepsakes. This listing is for one box.

input.descriptionHtml:
In Armagh, where the observatory has studied the night sky since 1789, a long leather case was the natural home for a spyglass: slim, hinged and kept within reach. This box borrows that shape for the things that clutter a desk or a side table. Keep it on a coffee table for the remotes and a pair of reading glasses, on a desk for envelopes and stamps, or on a hall console for keys and sunglasses. This listing is for one box.

input.descriptionHtml:
At Tarifa, the southern tip of mainland Europe, the sunset drink is a small ritual: a tray carried out to the terrace, with the mountains of Morocco in view across the strait. This leather tray is made for carrying that round of drinks. It holds glasses, a bottle and a bowl of olives in one trip, and its steel handles give a firm grip from the kitchen out to the terrace.

It is wood covered in leather, with each panel finished in neat topstitching, and slim leather straps hold the handles in place. At 19 by 15 inches it is roomy enough for a full round yet small enough to sit on an ottoman or a side table. The topstitching and straps are the kind of detail you notice each time you pick it up. It arrives ready to use.

Use it on an ottoman to gather remotes and coasters, on a sideboard as a small bar, or on a dresser to hold perfume bottles. This listing is for one tray.

input.title: BH | Premier Great Neck Shagreen Boxes, Set of 2
input.descriptionHtml:
In the early 1920s F. Scott Fitzgerald lived in Great Neck, on Long Island's North Shore, and the parties he saw there became the parties of West Egg in The Great Gatsby. These boxes are made for the small rituals of an evening like that: cufflinks set out before dressing, matches by the cocktail shaker, cards ready for a late game. Their shagreen-grained leather has the polish of the Jazz Age, and their compact size lets them sit neatly on a dresser, a bar or a desk.

Each box is covered in leather embossed with shagreen's fine pebbled grain and lined in paper inside. The two come as a pair, so they can sit side by side or be split between rooms, and they arrive ready to use.

Set one on a dresser for earrings and a watch and the other on a drink cart for matches and cocktail picks, or stack them on a desk for stamps, notecards and a good pen. This set includes two boxes.

input.descriptionHtml:
Armagh's observatory was founded in 1789 by Archbishop Richard Robinson, in an age when every fine instrument had a fitted case of its own. This box is made in the spirit of those fitted cases, for keeping small treasures together and safe. Its long, slim shape holds letters, pens and keepsakes in one place, and its lid closes over them so a desk or a shelf stays tidy.

It is wood covered in leather, standing on small brass feet and trimmed with nailheads set close together, with a brass chain detail and printed paper lining the inside. At 24 inches long and five deep it fits along the top of a bookcase or the back of a desk. It arrives ready to use.

Place it on a library shelf, a mantelpiece or a writing desk, holding old letters, a fountain pen and a pair of reading glasses. It also makes a handsome home for a few rolled maps or the photographs that never made it into an album. This listing is for one box.
